GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) reaches about **45.6% accuracy** when the key is at the 200th position of 300 key-value pairs. The paper doesn't state this number for that position directly; I derived it as follows.

- **What the text says:** Without query-aware contextualization, GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K)'s worst-case accuracy on the 300 key-value pair setting is 45.6% (page 8, referring to Figure 7).
- **What the figure shows:** In the 300 key-value pairs (~16K tokens) panel of Figure 7, the GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) curve hits its lowest point at the 200th position, at roughly 45% (page 7). The x-axis marks positions 1st, 50th, 100th, 150th, 200th, 250th and 300th.
- **The inference:** Since the curve's lowest point is at the 200th position, the stated 45.6% worst case is the accuracy at that position.

For comparison, the same model is near 100% when the key is at the start or end (Figure 7, page 7). With query-aware contextualization, it gets perfect accuracy on 300 key-value pairs (page 8).

There is no table of exact key-value results by position; the appendix tables cover only the multi-document QA task (page 18). So the 45.6% figure depends on reading the 200th position as the minimum on the plot.
